body.heading: Cut the sky shapes
paragraphs: Draw moons, stars, and planets on card and cut them out with your adult's help. Cover some in foil so they shine, and paint others bright colours.
A crescent moon is the trickiest shape. Draw a big circle, then cover part of it with another circle, and trace the banana shape that is left.

body.heading: Tie them on
paragraphs: Tie strings of different lengths to your shapes. Your adult ties the other ends along a stick or around a hoop.
Balance is the secret. If one side hangs lower, slide the strings until the mobile floats level, like a tiny solar system.

body.heading: Watch it turn
paragraphs: Hang your mobile where a gentle breeze from a door or window can reach it. It will turn slowly all by itself.
Real planets turn too, slowly and silently. Your mobile is a pocket model of the sky's slow dance.

takeaway: A balanced mobile of moons and stars turns gently in the air, just like the slow dance of the real sky.
safetyNotes: An adult should do or closely help with cutting and tying knots. Hang the mobile securely where it cannot fall, and never directly over a baby's cot.
screenFreeExtension: Lie under your mobile at bedtime and count the stars as they turn before you sleep.
